newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana finmin puts 1996/97 growth at 6.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Botswana finmin puts 1996/97 growth at 6.8 percent.

text.p: Botswana's Finance Minister Festus Mogae said on Monday that real gross domestic product was likely to grow by 6.8 percent in 1996/97 (April-March).
Presenting his annual budget, Mogae said the expansion was mainly due to the growth in the mining sector, dominated by the world's richest gem quality diamond mines.

And Mogae was upbeat about the future. "Long term prospects are favourable, with an increase in diamond production resulting from the continuous operations (at mines) and the Orapa mine expansion," Mogae said.

Continuous operations at Botswana's three diamond mines started on January 2 this year. Orapa will double treatment capacity to 17 million tonnes of kimberlite a year from the year 2000. The project will increase Botswana's annual diamond production from 17 million carats to 23 million carats.

Provisional statistics showed that growth in the real GDP had more than doubled from 3.1 per cent in 1994/95 to seven per cent in 1995/96, mainly due to increased diamond revenues as Jwaneng mine brought on a fourth production stream, he said.
"During that year, the mining sector, which accounts for about a third of GDP, grew by 9.9 percent," Mogae said.
"Preliminary estimates indicate that the balance of payments recorded an overall surplus of 848 million pula in 1996 compared to 591 million pula in the previous year," Mogae said.
This was 5.1 percent of GDP, against four percent in 1995.
This, and valuation gains arising from the depreciation of the pula, had grown Botswana's foreign exchange reserves by 39 percent to 18,410 million pula at the end of 1996.
"The foreign exchange reserves as at the end of 1996 were sufficient to finance about 29 months of imports of goods and services," Mogae said.
